intro: The structural multi-quarter thesis continues to strengthen through the post-FOMC turbulence. Three new developments this week reinforce the long-horizon picture: (1) Micron Q3 earnings confirmed for June 24 with consensus EPS $19.72 and revenue $34.52B (revised UP 3.1% in 30 days) — the buy-side community's collective endorsement that AI memory demand is intact and repricing upward even in a hawkish rate environment; (2) SK Hynix ADR SEC regulatory clearance now expected the week of June 22 (Nasdaq listing August 2026, ~$14B raise) — the structural conversion of a KRX-only asset into a globally accessible US-listed equity is the single most significant demand-side development since the HBM4E sample confirmation; (3) BTC has now produced four consecutive UTC days above $63,500 with the June 21 session low ($63,895.93) never testing the stop — the organic demand zone migration from $63,000–$63,500 to $63,500–$64,000+ demonstrates institutional accumulation consistent with the structural adoption thesis. The FOMC-driven dislocations in NVDA, META, MSFT, GOOGL, and AMZN remain multi-quarter structural accumulation opportunities. The AI infrastructure supercycle — driven by AI semis, AI memory, big-tech AI monetization, and Bitcoin's fixed-supply adoption ramp — has not been altered by Warsh's hawkish dots. The post-FOMC discount window is the structural entry point for investors with 2–4 year horizons.

ideas.name: NVIDIA
ideas.idea: The toll road on AI compute — June 24 dual catalyst (Annual Meeting + Micron Q3 on same day) is the most concentrated AI thesis validation event since February 2026 earnings; the FOMC discount is the structural accumulation window.
ideas.why: NVDA's $25B bond raise ($85B orders, 3.4x oversubscribed) is management's explicit declaration of AI capex continuity in a hawkish rate environment. Jensen Huang's 18-day Taiwan–South Korea trip ($150B annual spending commitment) demonstrates supply-chain construction at a multi-decade horizon. The June 24 compound event — Micron Q3 HBM demand data ($34.52B revenue consensus, up 3.1% in 30 days) arriving the same morning as Jensen's first post-FOMC public statements — creates a structural validation moment: if demand is intact (MU) AND management confidence is high (Jensen), the $195–$215 zone is the structural accumulation entry of the cycle. SK Hynix HBM4E 12-layer sample confirmation (48GB, 16Gbps per pin) and ADR listing approaching remove execution risk from the supply chain. The CUDA moat, Blackwell/Vera Rubin roadmap, SK Hynix supply locked through 2030, and $299 average analyst PT (62 analysts) create a multi-year structural bid.
ideas.driver: Hyperscaler + sovereign AI capex compounding through 2028+; inference demand following training ramp; Vera Rubin rack-scale systems entering production 2026–2027; HBM4E supply chain execution confirmed (SK Hynix 12-layer); CUDA ecosystem moat expanding into robotics and physical AI; $299 analyst consensus PT = 41.8% from current $210.69.
ideas.risk: Custom ASICs (Google TPU, AWS Trainium, Meta MTIA) erode H100/B200 share faster than expected in inference workloads; Micron Q3 miss on HBM signals AI memory demand cycle peaking before Vera Rubin ramp; Fed delivers multiple 2026 hikes creating sustained 30Y above 5.25% that structurally compresses AI-capex multiples sector-wide.

ideas.name: SK Hynix (000660.KS)
ideas.idea: 12-layer HBM4E samples confirmed; ADR Nasdaq listing August 2026 ($14B raise) converts KRX-only asset into globally accessible equity; HBM shortage extending through 2028; ₩2,000T market cap milestone unlocks new passive mandate category.
ideas.why: SK Hynix's structural position is unprecedented in Korean semiconductor history: 58% global HBM market share, official 12-layer HBM4E sample shipments confirmed (48GB, 16Gbps per pin, 20%+ power efficiency), NVIDIA supply partnership through 2030, 72% Q1 operating margin, ₩2,000T market cap milestone, ADR Nasdaq listing imminent (SEC clearance week of June 22, August 2026 listing, ~$14B raise). The ADR listing is the structural demand accelerator: it converts SK Hynix from a KRX-only asset into a global institutional equity accessible by US passive index funds, and the $14B raise creates a permanent structural demand event. The HBM4E shortage extending through 2028 means SK Hynix's pricing power in HBM4E (materially higher ASPs vs HBM4) has a 2+ year runway. Micron Q3 earnings June 24 (the week's HBM demand read-through) is the catalyst that resets SK Hynix's long-term thesis for buy-side desks worldwide.
ideas.driver: HBM4→4E product transition with SK Hynix the clear technology leader (58% share, 12-layer confirmed); shortage extending through 2028; NVIDIA supply lock; ADR Nasdaq listing August 2026 creating structural US demand channel ($14B); mandatory sell-side PT revision cascade from ₩2,690,000 to ₩3.0M+; KOSPI 9,000 passive inflow structural bid; potential ₩75T buyback.
ideas.risk: Samsung executes a credible HBM4E capacity ramp that captures a key NVIDIA qualification slot before SK Hynix completes customer qualification; ADR SEC clearance delayed materially (reducing near-term demand catalyst); AI capex cycle pauses in 2027 causing memory oversupply before the HBM4E shortage fully resolves.

ideas.name: Microsoft
ideas.idea: The lowest-risk path to enterprise AI monetization — FOMC selloff to ~$378 is a structural accumulation opportunity in the most recurring-revenue-driven megacap.
ideas.why: Microsoft's enterprise AI thesis is compounding: Azure AI workloads are inflecting, Copilot attach rates across hundreds of millions of enterprise seats are growing, and the OpenAI investment provides asymmetric exposure to frontier model development. At ~$378, the post-FOMC selloff offers the best entry since early 2026. The recurring-revenue enterprise model makes Microsoft the least DCF-sensitive megacap to rate uncertainty — cash flows are real, current, and contracted. June 24 AI capex validation from Micron Q3 + NVDA Annual Meeting is the secondary catalyst: confirmed AI capex durability from both the demand side (MU HBM revenue) and the supply-side confidence (Jensen capex commentary) is directly positive for Azure AI workload growth expectations. MSFT is the safest recovery vehicle for investors who want the AI monetization thesis without the tail risk of NVDA's gate-dependent add or BTC's stop-framework.
ideas.driver: Azure AI workload attach rates compounding; Copilot enterprise adoption across hundreds of millions of seats; OpenAI relationship providing frontier model access and differentiated enterprise AI; subscription model providing rate-insensitive contracted cash flows regardless of Warsh hawkish dots.
ideas.risk: AI capex-to-Azure-revenue monetization lag extends; antitrust scrutiny of the OpenAI relationship complicates the enterprise AI bundle; new AI-native infrastructure players (including SPCX's Cursor AI software layer) pull capital from 'mature AI' incumbents over a multi-year horizon.

ideas.name: Alphabet
ideas.idea: Cheapest full-stack AI at the megacap cohort's lowest forward multiple — search cannibalization risk still priced too harshly at ~$355; Micron Q3 AI demand confirmation on June 24 is the secondary catalyst for the whole AI megacap cohort.
ideas.why: Alphabet owns Gemini (frontier models), TPUs (cost-competitive inference at scale), Google Cloud (inflecting on enterprise AI), and search (generating cash for all of it). At ~$355 post-FOMC selloff, the forward multiple is the cheapest in the megacap cohort. The June 24 dual catalyst (Micron Q3 + NVDA Annual Meeting) is structurally positive for Alphabet: confirmed AI demand durability (MU HBM revenue) + Jensen AI capex commentary = the market re-rates the entire AI monetization cohort, with GOOGL as the lowest-multiple beneficiary. The TPU cost advantage in inference creates a structural pricing moat for Google Cloud AI workloads. If AI Overviews prove to be a search moat-extender rather than a cannibalization risk, the re-rating is a multi-year compounding opportunity that is currently priced as the worst-case scenario.
ideas.driver: TPU-driven inference cost advantage enabling competitive AI pricing; Gemini integration across billion-user surfaces; Google Cloud AI workload attach rates inflecting; potential search-moat expansion rather than cannibalization as AI Overviews extend session length and premium ad inventory.
ideas.risk: Genuine query erosion to AI assistants at scale; antitrust remedies fracturing the search + advertising bundle; higher-for-longer rates extend the multiple compression window before the AI Overviews thesis can compound; SPCX's Cursor AI creates a new channel through which developer tooling drives users toward non-Google AI interfaces.

ideas.name: SpaceX
ideas.idea: Generational franchise with triple-IG validation (Moody's Baa1, Fitch BBB+, S&P BBB); near-term step-aside after $185 stop trigger; watch for two consecutive closes above $185 on June 22+ before re-engaging the 3–5 year thesis.
ideas.why: SpaceX owns the only proven reusable orbital launch system at scale, Starlink at 5M+ subscribers growing ~40% annually, Starshield national-security contracts, and the AI coding platform Cursor (Anysphere, $60B stock acquisition, 1M+ developer users). The simultaneous investment-grade ratings from Moody's (Baa1, above Tesla's Baa3), Fitch (BBB+), and S&P (BBB) — issued within days of the IPO — are permanent franchise-quality anchors. The IG ratings validate cash flows that the rating agencies assessed independently; the equity market has not yet priced them (72+ hours of closure). SPX futures +0.74% and DXY ~100.23 create the best conditions for re-pricing the IG catalyst since the ratings were issued. The 3–5 year thesis: Starlink grows to $20B+ annualized revenue; Starship reduces cost-to-orbit by 10-50x creating a new satellite economy; Cursor AI adds a software revenue layer not in the IPO prospectus or IG rating models.
ideas.driver: Starlink subscriber and ARPU compounding toward $20B+ annualized revenue; Starship cost-to-orbit structural economics; Cursor AI software layer adding recurring developer-facing revenue; Starshield national-security base load; IG ratings permanently lowering cost of capital and expanding institutional buyer universe.
ideas.risk: IPO-cycle overvaluation requires sustained multiple compression before traditional value investors engage at scale; September 2 first earnings disappoints vs $2.4T implied expectations; key-person concentration risk (Elon Musk); December 9 lock-up expiry first major supply-side event; 84x revenue at $174.90 is the market's most extreme valuation multiple in US public equities.

ideas.name: Bitcoin
ideas.idea: Structural adoption thesis intact and strengthening — four consecutive UTC days above $63,500 stop with demand zone migrating higher ($63,178 → $63,895 session lows); IBIT outflows ended; DXY structural decline approaching; re-entry framework at $63,500+ is the cycle's structural accumulation window.
ideas.why: BTC's structural framework is strengthening organically. The four consecutive UTC sessions above $63,500 with progressively higher lows ($62,313 → $63,178 → $63,895) demonstrate institutional accumulation that is not thin-tape. The IBIT outflow streak ending ($86M net inflows, June 12) signals the institutional selling cycle is over. DXY declining from 101.13 (Juneteenth intraday) to 100.23 (Sunday) is FX markets pricing the Iran ceasefire Hormuz-reopening disinflation pathway — the exact macro sequence that precedes DXY structural decline and BTC structural recovery. The long-term thesis: fixed supply (21M BTC hard cap) × widening institutional access (IBIT, FBTC, combined $60B+ AUM) × halving cycle supply reduction (April 2024) × DXY structural decline (Hormuz → oil lower → CPI relief → rate pivot) = $75,000–$85,000 Q3–Q4 2026 target. BTC's multi-year thesis runs on halvings and institutional access, not FOMC meetings.
ideas.driver: Fixed supply meeting widening institutional access (ETFs at $60B+ AUM, corporate treasuries) across halving cycles; DXY structural decline as Hormuz reopening removes the oil-inflation driver that anchored dollar strength; IBIT inflows restarting signals institutional accumulation phase beginning; 'digital gold' narrative strengthening in a 'no forward guidance' Warsh policy regime where inflation uncertainty is elevated.
ideas.risk: Warsh actually delivers multiple 2026 rate hikes (not just aspirational dots), creating a sustained DXY above 103 that is structurally bearish for BTC over a 6-12 month horizon; IBIT inflow reversal proves to be short-lived; Strategy BTC sales signal corporate treasury accumulation thesis reversing; four consecutive UTC sessions above $63,500 masked by thin weekend tape — June 22 full-participation US session is the first real test of whether the demand zone migration is real.

ideas.name: Amazon
ideas.idea: AWS AI infrastructure winner + Hormuz reopening logistics tailwind — post-FOMC dip to ~$183 is the best entry in the megacap cloud cohort.
ideas.why: Amazon runs the world's largest commercial cloud (AWS), is ramping Trainium/Inferentia custom silicon to reduce AI inference costs, and has the logistics-and-Prime flywheel that scales into robotic AI. The FOMC-driven selloff of ~3.46% on June 17 brought AMZN to ~$183 — the most attractive valuation point in the megacap cloud cohort this year. The Iran ceasefire (Hormuz reopening) is a direct tailwind for Amazon's logistics economics — shipping cost inflation decreases as Hormuz commercial traffic normalizes, improving Prime delivery margins and fulfillment economics by an estimated 5–10%. Micron Q3 on June 24 is a secondary catalyst: AWS AI workload demand is confirmed by MU HBM revenue; if MU beats, AWS AI growth expectations re-rate upward. Trainium/Inferentia silicon creates a structural pricing moat for AWS AI workloads that reduces NVDA dependency while compounding over a 2–4 year horizon.
ideas.driver: AWS AI workload attach rates + Trainium/Inferentia inference cost advantage; Prime and logistics flywheel compounding at scale; Hormuz reopening reducing shipping cost inflation 5-10% for Amazon's logistics network; AI-native robotics expansion in fulfillment centers creating operational leverage.
ideas.risk: Cloud spending deceleration if enterprise IT budgets tighten in a persistently higher-rate environment; competitive pressure from Azure and Google Cloud on enterprise AI workload share; Trainium/Inferentia ramp timelines extending beyond 2027; logistics cost inflation reversing Hormuz-reopening gains if a new geopolitical supply disruption emerges.
